adjudication_note: Registry evidence is Sentinel-1 flood-extent acquisition over Doma/Makurdi/Guma on 25-26 Sep; inundation observation is not onset.
Corroborating Guardian report published 26 Sep states residents woke the previous morning to serious flooding in Lokoja; frozen 28 Sep timestamp is a later already-submerged report.
NEMA/BYSEMA carried out an assessment following a flood report and listed Akenfa as affected; 30 Sep is an assessment/documentation date without a first-impact onset.
MAN leadership assessed massive flood devastation on 21 Oct; source states affected industries had suspended production for weeks, proving the registry date is not flood onset.
Jigawa state report describes widespread season-long destruction, displacement and ongoing assessment and lists Hadejia among badly affected LGAs; no onset date is established.
Guardian says heavy downpour occurred at the weekend before Monday 10 Jul and market remained flooded when visited; onset is bounded to the preceding weekend rather than 10 Jul documentation date.
PUNCH reports rain began around 10pm Sunday, intensified around 4am Monday 4 Sep and flooding occurred Monday morning.
Students reported flooded hostels, repeated sleepless nights and a flood problem that had lingered; 14 Sep protest/report date does not establish first impact.
Statement says communities were already going through hardship caused by flood; no onset or bounded first-impact interval is supplied.
Federal situation briefing listed Makurdi among LGAs already submerged following rainfall; briefing date is not established onset.
Federal situation briefing listed Onitsha North among LGAs already submerged following rainfall; briefing date is not established onset.
The Sun reports heavy rain on Monday 8 Jul caused flash floods in several Yenagoa locations; report was published 9 Jul.
Vanguard reports close to 12 hours of torrential rainfall beginning Thursday night and continuing into Friday morning, leaving Makurdi areas submerged.
Channels reports statewide flooding after days of relentless rainfall and ten affected LGAs; exact Hadejia first-impact time is unresolved.
7 Sep is the exact date of a drowning incident in an already flooded Hadejia river. It dates the incident, not the flood onset.
PUNCH reports heavy rains persisted Tuesday to Wednesday and several Yenagoa neighbourhoods were submerged by flash floods.
PUNCH reports rain began around 3am Monday 14 Oct, continued until noon, and several Makurdi areas flooded that day.
NEMA visit occurred during active flood response with rescue/evacuation, shelters and displaced persons already in place; no onset is established.
7 Nov report describes continuing high/rising water; a 30 Oct PUNCH report already documented inundated Yenagoa-area communities, so 7 Nov is materially later than onset.
